purpose: Teach: あゆみ/つきあっ/すさまじい/このほど/とかく/ぬけ/かれこれ/めちゃめちゃ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんと長いあゆみだったぞ
lines.en: You know, Gran, when your father was young, we took a long walk together.
lines.style: Quiet, reaching back into memory. Slow unhurried pace. Soft voiced, as if speaking to the memory itself as much as to her. A small pause between phrases, letting time settle.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃんとは長くつきあってこられたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, dear — you and Grandfather did have a long life together, didn't you?
lines.style: Warm, affirming nod in the voice. Gentle rhythm. Speaking as someone who has watched the years accumulate and finds them good. Slight lift at the end, inviting him to continue.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがすさまじい台風を語られたぞ
lines.en: Gran, I remember your father telling us about the most terrible typhoon when we were young.
lines.style: A flicker of something urgent beneath the quietness — the power of that old storm still present in his voice. Measured but alive. Slight emphasis on the memory's weight.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、このほど勲章を授与されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Oh, your father received a commendation not long ago, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Gentle correction or gentle addition to what he's said — the warm voice of someone who has their own memories to weave in. A small lilt of pride. Conversational, not intrusive.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、お父さんはとかく無口だったぞ
lines.en: Gran, your father was always a quiet man, you know.
lines.style: Acknowledging something true and fixed. Quiet respect in the voice for that quietness. Not sad, not judging — just stating something that was. Even tempo, steady as his recollection.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、たまにふっと頭からぬけちゃう事、おありだったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and sometimes you'd just lose a thought mid-sentence, wouldn't you, dear?
lines.style: A small, knowing laugh beneath the words. Tender affection for his absent-mindedness. Spoken with the ease of someone who loved him through it. Warm, not mocking.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんとかれこれ五十年連れ添ったぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I think of it now — nearly fifty years we walked through life together.
lines.style: The full weight of time settling into his voice. Slow, deliberate. A man counting something precious and finding it real. Trailing slightly at the end, as if the years themselves stretch out behind the words.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、書道がめちゃめちゃ綺麗だったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: His calligraphy was so beautiful, wasn't it, dear? I can still see it so clearly.
lines.style: Eyes half-closed in the voice, seeing again. Warm, almost surprised at how vivid the memory still is. A slow, appreciative breath. Intimate, as though she's showing him what she sees.
